reassessment_conclusion.reason: The corpus supports the two-projection field structure but shows insufficient stable coverage in every pre-audit semantic family except no family reaches both complete coverage and production-level repeatability.

readiness_findings.evidence: Weighted exact-span recall 0.697 and the strongest family repeatability, but later operative questions were missed or replaced by earlier decision-choice questions in several cases.
Weighted exact-span recall 0.614, but derivation-mode serialization preserves turn references without the exact excerpts that justified the derivation.
Weighted recall 0.545; 10 of 22 gold stance observations were never recovered and relation labels were less repeatable than their spans.
Weighted recall 0.479; material later corrections and joint-decision pressure were often captured under a neighboring family or missed as pressure.
Weighted recall 0.472 and family span repeatability 0.384; 24 of 92 non-Case-01 raw candidates named an invalid source and one used an invalid quote.
Dropped-thread weighted recall 0.273 with only 2 of 11 gold observations stable, even though selected thread spans were often repeatable.
Option-family repeatability was moderate, but explicit options, thresholds, and stop or delay conditions were repeatedly omitted.
A source reference must preserve the exact excerpt or offsets for every derivation component; turn-only derivation references cannot receive exact-span grounding credit.
This experiment evaluates pre-audit conversation understanding. Defer, release, privacy, and review-status decisions remain timing and policy boundaries, not corpus-validated quality claims.
